enriched.title: Simple Past e Vocabulário de Frequência e Tratamento
enriched.summary: A aula aborda o uso do Simple Past e expressões de frequência, quantidade e duração, além de vocabulário relacionado à medicina e tratamentos. Também são exploradas construções no futuro e exemplos práticos para fixação.
mainTopics: Uso do futuro com 'will' e 'going to'

vocabulary.definition: To move or travel toward a particular place.
examples: Why didn’t he come to work today? (Por que ele não veio trabalhar hoje?)
He came to the meeting on time. (Ele chegou à reunião no horário.)

vocabulary.definition: Used to ask about the frequency of an action or event.
examples: How often did he go to the hospital for treatment? (Com que frequência ele ía ao hospital para tratamento?)

vocabulary.definition: A substance used to treat disease or injury; the science or practice of diagnosing and treating illnesses.
examples: Many people are taking Ozempic and other similar medicines. (Muitas pessoas estão tomando Ozempic e outros remédios similares.)

vocabulary.definition: Used to ask about the duration of an action or event.
examples: How long did you work at Nestlé? (Quanto tempo você trabalhou na Nestlé?)

vocabulary.definition: Used to ask about the number of occurrences of an action or event.
examples: How many times did he repeat the same information during the presentation? (Quantas vezes ele repetiu a mesma informação durante a apresentação?)

grammar.explanation: Used to describe actions or events that happened in the past.
rules: Regular verbs end in -ed in the past tense.
Irregular verbs have unique past forms (e.g., 'come' becomes 'came').
Use 'did' + base form for negatives and questions.
examples: The hotel had a swimming pool but it didn’t have a restaurant.
Why didn’t he come to work today?
How often did he go to the hospital for treatment?
commonMistakes: Using the base form instead of the past form in affirmative sentences (e.g., 'He come' instead of 'He came').
Adding -ed to irregular verbs (e.g., 'comed' instead of 'came').

grammar.explanation: 'Will' is used for predictions or decisions made at the moment of speaking, while 'going to' is used for planned actions or events that seem certain to happen.
rules: Use 'will' + base verb for spontaneous decisions or predictions.
Use 'am/is/are going to' + base verb for planned actions or evidence-based predictions.
examples: I think that it will rain tomorrow.
I think that it is going to rain tomorrow.
Look at the sky. Is it going to rain?
commonMistakes: Confusing 'will' and 'going to' in contexts where one is more appropriate.
Using 'will' for planned actions (e.g., 'I will go to the party' instead of 'I am going to the party').

expressions.usage: Used to introduce unverified information or gossip.
examples: There is (a) rumor that says (that) Trump will die before the end of his term. (Tem um boato que diz que Trump vai morrer antes de terminar seu mandato.)

practiceQuestions.question: Translate: 'Por que ele não veio trabalhar hoje?'
practiceQuestions.answer: Why didn’t he come to work today?
practiceQuestions.explanation: The question is in the Simple Past, so 'didn't' is used with the base form of the verb 'come'.

practiceQuestions.question: Fill in the blank: 'How ___ did you work at Nestlé?'
practiceQuestions.explanation: 'How long' is used to ask about the duration of an action.

practiceQuestions.question: Choose the correct form: 'John never ___ his wife when he has a problem.'
practiceQuestions.explanation: The sentence is in the Present Simple, so 'tells' is the correct conjugation for 'John' (third person singular).

culturalNotes: In English-speaking cultures, discussing medical topics like treatments or medications is often done with caution to respect privacy and sensitivity.
Expressions like 'How often' and 'How long' are commonly used in both formal and informal contexts, making them essential for day-to-day conversations.
studyTips: Memorize the conjugations of irregular verbs by practicing them in sentences.
Use flashcards to study expressions like 'how often' and 'how long'.
Practice forming questions in the Simple Past to improve fluency.
originalExamples: Our team not always wins. (Nosso time nem sempre vence.)
The hotel had a swimming pool but it didn’t have a restaurant. (O hotel tinha uma piscina mas não tinha um restaurante.)
Why didn’t he come to work today? (Por que ele não veio trabalhar hoje?)
How often did he go to the hospital for treatment? (Com que frequência ele ía ao hospital para tratamento?)
She promises that she will arrive at the meeting on time. (Ela promete que chegará à reunião no horário.)
I think that it will rain tomorrow. (Acho que vai chover amanhã.)
I think that it is going to rain tomorrow. (Acho que vai chover amanhã.)
John never tells his wife when he has a problem. (John nunca diz à esposa quando tem um problema.)
How long did you work at Nestlé? (Quanto tempo você trabalhou na Nestlé?)
How many employees are there in your department? (Quantos funcionários tem no seu departamento?)
Look at the sky. Is it going to rain? (Olhe o céu. Vai chover?)
It’s 9.00 pm and the lawyers are still working. Is there any exceptional case this week? (São 9 da noite e os advogados ainda estão trabalhando. Tem algum caso excepcional esta semana?)
Yesterday, my friend and I bought tickets for the game next Sunday. (Ontem, meu amigo e eu compramos ingressos para o jogo no próximo domingo.)
Our team has the best players of the season. We’re going to win. (Nosso time tem os melhores jogadores da temporada. Nós vamos ganhar.)
I don’t believe that we’ll colonize Mars. (Eu não acredito que colonizaremos Marte.)
There is (a) rumor that says (that) Trump will die before ending / before the end of his term. (Tem um boato que diz que Trump vai morrer antes de terminar seu mandato.)
Who is going to the conference with us? (Quem vai à conferência conosco?)
How many times did he repeat the same information during the presentation? (Quantas vezes ele repetiu a mesma informação durante a apresentação?)
Many people are taking Ozempic and other similar medicines. (Muitas pessoas estão tomando Ozempic e outros remédios similares.)
My aunt lost 15 kilos taking Mounjaro. (Minha tia perdeu 15 quilos tomando Mounjaro.)
When are you going to start your treatment? (Quando você vai começar seu tratamento?)
She said (that) you found a new job last month. (Ela disse que você encontrou um novo emprego no mês passado.)
